To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

business processes should be modelled using a simulation tool that supports the modelling and analysis of inter-organizational business systems, is capable of handling a large number of decision makers and decision making levels, is able to provide multi-level outputs and has an easy to use graphical interface.

(a) business processes are a special type of processes and have their own characteristics; (b) business processes are not only affected by internal but also by external factors; (c) inter-organisation business processes require a different approach to simulation modelling than intra-organisation processes; (d) inter-organisations simulation modelling requires multi-level analysis; (e) inter-organizational simulation modelling requires multi-user analysis.

(1) Business processes are complex and dynamic, (2) Business process modelling is a multi-level activity and (3) Business process modelling tools should be able to handle the complexity of inter-organizational processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the requirements and problems in business process modelling and simulation.
the identification of the characteristics and requirements for the simulation of intra- and interorganisational business processes.
the modelling of business processes in a multi-organisational setting, and the development of simulation packages that can be used for this purpose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
business simulation is not yet a fully developed discipline, although it has a lot of potential for practical application.
simulation can be a powerful tool for business redesign but its effectiveness is highly dependent upon the quality of modelling and the appropriateness of the simulation package used.

simulation is a powerful tool for modelling business processes, and that the problems encountered in modelling are mainly of a practical nature, which could be overcome through the development of appropriate software tools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
simulation can be effectively used in business redesign, but that the modelling process is not straightforward and should be carefully planned and executed.

business process modelling should be considered as a part of the business process change management cycle and that simulation can be a useful tool for this purpose, especially for the analysis of inter-organizational business processes.
simulation can be a very powerful tool for business process redesign, but that its use in inter-organisations is still at a very early stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current state of the art of business process modelling and simulation is not yet mature enough for the modelling of complex inter-organisional business systems.
simulation is a powerful tool for modelling business systems, and that it can provide a useful framework for business process redesign.

the modelling requirements for business process simulation are different from those of manufacturing process simulation, and that the simulation tools used for business process modelling should be designed accordingly.
